I've been farming this land in Quzhou for four decades. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know when to water, I know what the weather usually does. My wife and I manage most of it ourselves — my son sends money from the city but he doesn't come back for the busy seasons anymore. So I plan for what two old people can actually handle.

My 10.1 mu: I keep 7 mu in the wheat-maize double crop rotation — that's my stable income, the crop I can predict. The remaining 3.1 mu goes to cotton. Cotton prices have been up and down, but I've grown it for thirty years and I'm not about to stop now. It pays better per mu when the market is good.

**Wheat (7 mu, winter):** I'll plant "Jimai 22" — same improved variety I've used for six years. I know how it behaves. I'll rotary-till after maize harvest in October, apply base fertilizer before planting. Three irrigations: one at sowing to get germination, one at jointing in April, one at heading. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in winter, then aphid and powdery mildew spray in May. I'll push 480 jin per mu if the spring rains cooperate.

**Maize (7 mu, summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I direct-seed into the stubble — no-till saves me a day of work and keeps moisture in. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, always have. Heavy nitrogen at tasseling is the key. Two irrigations only — electricity for the pump is expensive, and summer usually brings enough rain if I pick my timing. I expect 600 jin per mu.

**Cotton (3.1 mu, spring):** I deep plough this plot in March, transplant seedlings in late April. Bt hybrid cotton — it's cut my pesticide costs on bollworm over the years, though I still spray five times for other pests. Cotton needs four waterings across the season. Nitrogen goes in multiple splits — base, bud stage, flowering, boll setting. I aim for 300 jin of seed cotton per mu. It's hard work picking in September but I manage.
